items.title: Fourier sample from a generalized-dihedral reflection coset state
items.statement:
Write $A=\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ additively, $N\ge2$, and identify its generalized-dihedral group with $A\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ under
$$
(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',\,b+b'\bmod2).
$$
Let $H_s=\{(0,0),(s,1)\}$ and let a total encoded function $F$ be constant on each left coset of $H_s$ and distinct on different left cosets. Start in the uniform state on the $2N$ group elements, evaluate the coherent XOR oracle for $F$ into a zero output register, discard that register, apply the positive-sign $\operatorname{QFT}_N$ to the first coordinate, and measure that coordinate. The measured $k\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ is uniform. Conditional on $k$, the remaining qubit is, up to a global phase,
$$
|\psi_k\rangle=\frac{|0\rangle+\exp(2\pi i ks/N)|1\rangle}{\sqrt2}.
$$

The coordinate readout uses the Lüders projective instrument for the projections $\Pi_k=|k\rangle\langle k|\otimes I_2$. The stated conditional qubit is the post-measurement state after discarding the measured coordinate.
items.axiom_use: None; all registers and sums are finite.

items.title: Finite cyclic discrete-logarithm problem and costed encoding
Hidden shift as generalized-dihedral hidden subgroup
items.statement:
Let $A$ be a finite abelian group in explicit additive coordinates, and let $f,g:A\to S$ satisfy the hidden-shift promise of [[def-qa-finite-abelian-hidden-shift-problem]]: both maps are injective and there is a unique $s\in A$ such that $f(a)=g(a+s)$ for every $a$. Write $D_A=A\rtimes\mathbb Z_2$ with
$$
(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',b+b'\bmod2),
$$
and define $F(a,0)=f(a)$ and $F(a,1)=g(a)$. Then $F$ is constant exactly on the left cosets of the order-two subgroup $H_s=\{(0,0),(s,1)\}=\langle(s,1)\rangle$. The subgroup determines the shift uniquely: $H_s=H_t$ implies $s=t$.

If a coherent XOR oracle for this $F$ is directly supplied, one $F$-oracle query implements one value query. From only coherent XOR oracles for $f$ and $g$, the $F$-XOR operation can be implemented with four calls total (two to compute the values into scratch registers and two to uncompute them), plus the controlled output XOR; no controlled call to either oracle is assumed. All gate, workspace, and named-oracle query costs remain separately charged.
items.axiom_use: None; all groups, functions, and encodings are finite.

items.title: Power-of-two dihedral hidden-subgroup sieve
items.statement:
Input an integer $n\ge1$, $N=2^n$, and either (i) a coherent XOR oracle $O_F$ for a total encoded function $F:D_N\to S$ that is constant on each left coset of the unknown reflection subgroup $H_s=\langle yx^s\rangle$ and takes distinct values on different left cosets, or (ii) a finite cyclic hidden-shift instance on $A=\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z$ together with its reflection oracle constructed by [[thm-qa-hidden-shift-generalized-dihedral-reduction]]. Use coordinates $(a,b)\in\mathbb Z/N\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z$ with multiplication $(a,b)(a',b')=(a+(-1)^b a',b+b')$ and fix $x=(-1,0)$ and $y=(0,1)$; then $yx^s=(s,1)$. Charge each supplied or constructed oracle call according to its interface.

Every projective readout below is implemented by the Lüders instrument of its stated projections. Charge each supplied measurement or instrument implementation under its declared interface.

For $n\le5$, query all group elements (at most $2N\le64$ values of $F$) and return the unique $s$ for which $F(0,0)=F(s,1)$. For $n\ge6$, set $m=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$ once and retain this $m$ through all recursive calls. The following procedure is run at modulus $2^r$, starting with $r=n$:

1. If $r\le5$, use the direct-query base case. Otherwise set $t_r=\lceil(r-1)/m\rceil$ and create a list $L_0$ of $M=3\cdot2^{3m}$ independent coset samples: prepare the uniform group state with Hadamards on its $r+1$ coordinate bits, evaluate $O_F$, discard the function-output register, apply the positive-sign $\operatorname{QFT}_{2^r}$ to the cyclic coordinate and measure that coordinate. Store the measured label $k$ and retain its conditional qubit $|\psi_k\rangle=(|0\rangle+e^{2\pi i k s/2^r}|1\rangle)/\sqrt2$.
2. For each $j=0,\ldots,t_r-1$, put $w_j=\min(m,r-1-mj)$. The current labels are divisible by $2^{mj}$. Bucket them by the $w_j$ bits of $k/2^{mj}$ immediately above those trailing zeroes, using only the lower $r-1$ bits of $k$. In each bucket, preserve current list order, pair consecutive entries, and leave the last entry unmatched if the bucket has odd size; this is a maximum-cardinality disjoint matching. For each pair, apply the CNOT pair combiner and measure its second qubit with the Lüders instrument. Retain only outcome $1$; the retained state has label $k-\ell\pmod {2^r}$. Discard unmatched states and outcome-$0$ states. The next list consists of the retained states.
3. The widths sum to $r-1$, so every final label is $0$ or $2^{r-1}$. If a state with label $2^{r-1}$ occurs, measure its qubit in the $\{|+\rangle,| -\rangle\}$ basis. Outcome $+$ means $s$ is even; outcome $-$ means $s$ is odd. If the target label is absent, return FAIL.
4. For even $s$, put $r'=r-1$, $x'=x^2$, $y'=y$, and $s'=s/2$. Identify child coordinates with $K_0=\langle x^2,y\rangle$ by
$$\phi_0:\mathbb Z/2^{r'}\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad \phi_0(a',b')=(2a',b')\pmod {2^r}.$$
Use the child oracle $F_0=F\circ\phi_0$ and run this procedure at modulus $2^{r'}$. A coherent $F_0$ query is implemented by appending a fresh clean low address bit $0$ to the $r'$ bits of $a'$, retaining $b'$, and making one parent $O_F$ call.

   For odd $s$, put $r'=r-1$, $x'=x^2$, $y'=yx$, and $s'=(s-1)/2$. Identify child coordinates with $K_1=\langle x^2,yx\rangle$ by
$$\phi_1:\mathbb Z/2^{r'}\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z\longrightarrow\mathbb Z/2^r\mathbb Z\times\mathbb Z/2\mathbb Z, \qquad \phi_1(a',b')=(2a'+b',b')\pmod {2^r}.$$
Use $F_1=F\circ\phi_1$ and recurse at modulus $2^{r'}$. To implement a coherent $F_1$ query, append a fresh clean low address bit $z=0$, copy $b'$ to $z$ by CNOT, make one parent $O_F$ call on the ambient address $(a',z,b')$, and uncopy $z$ by the same CNOT. Thus each child hiding-oracle query uses one parent $F$ query; the odd embedding adds two ordinary CNOT gates per query, and the even embedding adds none beyond the clean address wire. Return $2s'$ in the even branch and $2s'+1$ in the odd branch.

   Before the recursive call, discard the current sample, pair, output, and label registers after recording the parity branch; carry only the classical branch result and recursion parameters. The child call reuses this workspace.

The exact sampling-state law and pair-combination identity are in [[lem-qa-dihedral-coset-state-fourier-law]] and [[lem-qa-dihedral-sieve-pair-combination]]. The correctness, error, and resource claims for this locally specified shortened-final-width version are proved in [[thm-qa-dihedral-sieve-scope]]. The procedure is only specified for power-of-two cyclic orders; no arbitrary-$N$ or arbitrary finite-abelian extension is asserted.

items.title: Clean reversible controlled multiplication by a cyclic constant
items.statement:
Let $G=\langle g\rangle$ have order $q\ge2$, let $c\in G$, and let valid fixed-length codes occupy a subset $V\subseteq\{0,1\}^w$. Suppose total Boolean circuits are supplied for functions $h_c,h_{c^{-1}}:\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}^w\to\{0,1\}^w$, where
$$h_c(b,z)=\begin{cases}z,&b=0,\\\operatorname{enc}(u c),&b=1,\ z=\operatorname{enc}(u)\in V,\\z,&b=1,\ z\notin V,\end{cases}.$$
For each fixed control $b$, the maps $z\mapsto h_c(b,z)$ and $z\mapsto h_{c^{-1}}(b,z)$ are inverse permutations; the full controlled permutation preserves $b$.
Then reversible embedding supplies a clean-ancilla circuit that acts on a control bit and accumulator by
$$
|b,z,0_{\mathrm{work}}\rangle\longmapsto |b,h_c(b,z),0_{\mathrm{work}}\rangle.
$$
If the two Boolean circuits have at most $S$ non-input nodes and $E$ port uses each, the construction uses at most $12S+8E+5w$ elementary gates and at most $2(S+E)+w$ clean work wires. The gate charge counts each supplied $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli as one gate; no cost for constructing the Boolean descriptions is inferred.
items.axiom_use: None; the construction is a finite Boolean circuit and a finite basis calculation.

items.title: Kuperberg dihedral hidden-subgroup scope and resource claim
items.statement:
Let $n\ge1$ and $N=2^n$. Let $F:D_N\to S$ be a total encoded function that is constant on each left coset of $H_s=\langle yx^s\rangle$ and takes distinct values on different left cosets, accessed by a coherent XOR oracle either directly or through [[thm-qa-hidden-shift-generalized-dihedral-reduction]]. Equivalently, $F(u)=F(v)$ exactly when $uH_s=vH_s$, as required by [[alg-qa-dihedral-hidden-subgroup-sieve]]. Use the Lüders instruments specified there for the projective readouts. For $n\le5$ the direct branch succeeds exactly with at most $64$ $F$ queries. For $n\ge6$, put $m=\lceil\sqrt{n-1}\rceil$ and $M=3\cdot2^{3m}$. The locally specified shortened-final-width sieve has failure probability at most
$$\min\{1,nm\exp(-2^{m/3-1})\}.$$
It uses at most $nM+64$ named $F$-oracle queries, $O(n^3M)$ ideal gates for sieve control and recursive coordinate maps, $O(n^2m^2M)$ classical bit operations for label sorting and list processing, $O(M+n+w_F+a_F)$ quantum workspace, and $O(nM)$ bits to store all active labels. Here $w_F$ is the output-register width and $a_F$ is additional workspace for the supplied or constructed $F$ implementation. The $O(n^3M)$ gate count excludes the implementation of the named $F$ interface itself. An explicit $F$ circuit using $G_F(n)$ gates per call adds $O((nM+64)G_F(n))$ gates. If $F$ is constructed from only the two coherent XOR oracles for a hidden-shift pair, each call uses four $f/g$ oracle calls and adds $O(w_F)$ ordinary gates for controlled output selection; add $O((nM+64)w_F)$ selector gates, and charge any explicit circuits implementing $f$ and $g$ separately.

Since $m=\Theta(\sqrt n)$, the named $F$-query count, sieve gate count, and classical label-processing count are $2^{O(\sqrt n)}=2^{O(\sqrt{\log_2 N})}$ up to polynomial factors in $n$. The total workspace and any oracle-implementation gate costs retain the explicit interface-dependent terms above. The theorem is confined to power-of-two cyclic orders and supplied exact interfaces. It proves no polynomial-time claim, no arbitrary-$N$ version, and no algorithm for arbitrary finite abelian hidden shift.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite matching, finite probability, and the stated oracle model.

items.title: Costed coherent evaluation of cyclic group powers
items.statement:
Inputs are a valid instance from [[def-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm-problem]], exponent registers $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, and one of these access profiles:

1. a supplied coherent XOR oracle for $f(u,v)=g^u x^v$; initialize a fresh output target to $0^w$, invoke the oracle once, and return its output (the zero target need not be the encoding of the group identity); or
2. explicit reversible group-operation circuits, or separately charged named controlled-multiplication operations with the same complete-register action, for each classically specified constant and its inverse. Initialize a fresh accumulator to $\operatorname{enc}(e)$, the code of the group identity. Precompute $g_j=g^{2^j}$ and $x_j=x^{2^j}$ for $0\le j<L$, where $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, by repeated squaring. For $j=0,\ldots,L-1$, use the bit $u_j$ to apply the clean controlled multiplication by $g_j$ to the accumulator, and use $v_j$ to apply the clean controlled multiplication by $x_j$. The procedure is the circuit of [[lem-qa-controlled-cyclic-multiplication-clean]] applied at each control bit.

In profile 2, return the accumulator as the function value. The exponent registers are unchanged, all work and temporary target wires are returned to their declared initial states, and each direct oracle invocation or group-operation invocation is charged under its separately declared access profile. If only an uncontrolled black-box group operation is supplied, return UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS: it does not provide a controlled call.

To supply the total coherent XOR oracle required by the hidden-subgroup sampler, profile 2 is wrapped as follows. Prepare its $w$-bit accumulator from zero to $\operatorname{enc}(e)$ with at most $w$ Pauli-$X$ gates, execute the $2L$ controlled multiplications, copy the resulting $w$-bit value by CNOT into an arbitrary target $y$, then reverse the evaluation using the separately supplied inverse-constant controlled multiplications. Finally undo the initial $X$ gates. This implements $|u,v,y\rangle\mapsto|u,v,y\oplus\operatorname{enc}(g^ux^v)\rangle$ on valid exponent codes and restores every auxiliary wire to zero. The supplied total controlled operations also define its action on invalid exponent codes; these values are the declared Boolean extension. The wrapper uses $4L$ controlled multiplications and at most $3w$ extra $X$/CNOT gates; preparation, output copying, and inverse calls are charged.

items.title: Correctness and clean-work cost of cyclic power evaluation
items.statement: For every valid encoded cyclic-group input $(G,g,x,q)$ with $q\ge2$ and every $u,v\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$, the explicit-circuit branch of [[alg-qa-cyclic-group-power-evaluation]] writes the encoding of $g^u x^v$ into the accumulator, leaves the exponent registers unchanged, and returns every clean work and temporary target register to zero. If $L=\lceil\log_2 q\rceil$ and each controlled multiplication by a known constant has gate cost at most $C_G$, the circuit uses $2L$ controlled multiplications and $O(LC_G)$ gates per evaluation, in addition to the separately charged classical precomputation. The compute-XOR-uncompute wrapper in that algorithm implements the full target-XOR action on valid exponent codes, with its declared total extension elsewhere. If each forward and inverse-constant controlled multiplication costs at most $C_G$, that wrapper uses $4L$ such calls and at most $3w$ additional $X$/CNOT gates, hence $O(LC_G+w)$ gates, and restores its auxiliary registers to zero.
items.axiom_use: None; the proof uses finite binary expansions and group-power identities.

items.title: Finite cyclic discrete logarithm by Fourier sampling
items.statement:
Input a promised instance $(G,g,x,q)$ from [[def-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm-problem]] and a rational confidence target $\delta=p/v$ supplied as binary positive integers $p<v$, together with supplied exact uniform-state preparation and product-QFT circuits for $\mathbb Z_q^2$, including their full-register extensions and declared costs as required by [[alg-qa-finite-abelian-hidden-subgroup-sample]]. If the direct coherent $f$ oracle is unavailable, first check that the supplied interfaces support profile 2 of [[alg-qa-cyclic-group-power-evaluation]], including classical repeated squaring and the forward and inverse-constant controlled multiplications. If they do not, return `UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS` before sampling. Otherwise construct that profile's explicit compute-XOR-uncompute oracle and precompute its repeated-squaring constants once for all samples.
Let $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, computed as the bit length of $q-1$. Let $D$ be the least integer $d\ge0$ with $2^d\delta\ge1$, found by testing $d=0,1,\ldots$ using exact rational comparisons, and set $t=(1+L)D$.
Repeat the following $t$ times, with fresh registers and independent measurements:

1. Use [[alg-qa-finite-abelian-hidden-subgroup-sample]] once on $\mathbb Z_q\times\mathbb Z_q$ with hiding function $f(u,v)=g^ux^v$, obtaining a character label $(c,d)$.
2. Use [[alg-qa-euclidean-modular-inverse]] on $(q,c)$. If it returns `NO_INVERSE`, discard this sample and continue; otherwise its output is $c^{-1}\pmod q$.
3. Set $\widetilde a=d\,c^{-1}\pmod q$.
4. Compute $g^{\widetilde a}$ by binary repeated squaring using the supplied multiplication interface, then compare it with $x$ using the equality interface. Return $\widetilde a$ only if they agree.

If no iteration returns a verified value, return FAIL. A direct coherent oracle for $f$ costs one $f$ query per sample only when explicitly supplied; on the supported fallback branch, charge the controlled group operations, gates, and classical precomputation of [[alg-qa-cyclic-group-power-evaluation]]. The algorithm does not infer controlled access from an uncontrolled oracle.

items.title: Finite cyclic discrete-log correctness, success and costs
items.statement:
Let $G=\langle g\rangle$ have known exact order $q\ge2$, let $x=g^a$, and let $\delta=p/v$ be supplied as binary positive integers $p<v$. Write $K$ for the sum of their bit lengths. For an access profile of [[alg-qa-finite-cyclic-discrete-logarithm]] supplying either the direct coherent $f$ oracle or the complete supported power-evaluation fallback, every returned exponent is verified and equals the unique $a\in\{0,\ldots,q-1\}$. If neither is supplied, the procedure returns `UNSUPPORTED_ACCESS` before sampling; the following sampling, success and cost guarantees concern the supported profiles. Each independent Fourier sample succeeds with probability $\varphi(q)/q\ge1/(1+\log_2q)$. Put $L=\lceil\log_2q\rceil$, let $D$ be the least integer $d\ge0$ with $2^d\delta\ge1$, and set $t=(1+L)D$. With $t$ samples, the probability of returning the exact answer is at least $1-\delta$.

Let $w$ be the supplied group-element encoding width. A direct coherent function-oracle profile uses at most $O(L(1+\ln(1/\delta)))$ function queries and separately uses $O(L(1+\ln(1/\delta)))$ ordinary multiplication/equality operations for classical verification. If $f$ is implemented by controlled group multiplications, there are $O(L^2(1+\ln(1/\delta)))$ controlled-multiplication calls and the same order of ordinary multiplication/equality calls for verification. If the explicitly supplied reversible multiplication, equality, and both forward and inverse-constant controlled-multiplication circuits each cost at most $C_G$ gates and the supplied exact uniform preparation and product QFT cost $O(L^2)$ ideal gates, the total ideal gate count is
$$
O\!\left((L^2C_G+Lw+L^3)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).
$$
If one classical multiplication or equality operation on the encoding costs at most $T_G$ bit operations and modular inverses use the schoolbook extended-Euclidean algorithm, the classical bit cost of confidence preprocessing, arithmetic and verification is
$$
O\!\left(K^2+(L^2T_G+L^4)(1+\ln(1/\delta))\right).
$$
All query, gate, and classical bit bounds are conditional on the stated supplied interfaces. The exact binary QFT is counted in the ideal-gate model; no finite-set compilation cost or generic efficient group encoding is asserted.
items.axiom_use: None; all samples and all arithmetic procedures are finite.

items.title: Hidden-shift left cosets in a generalized dihedral group
items.statement:
Take $A=\mathbb Z/4\mathbb Z$, shift $s=1$, and define injective maps $f(a)=a$ and $g(b)=b-1\pmod4$. Then $f(a)=g(a+1)$ for every $a$. With the generalized-dihedral product law and $H_1=\langle(1,1)\rangle$, the left cosets are $C_0=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}$, $C_1=\{(1,0),(2,1)\}$, $C_2=\{(2,0),(3,1)\}$, and $C_3=\{(3,0),(0,1)\}$.
The function $F(a,0)=f(a)$, $F(a,1)=g(a)$ takes the common value $a$ on $C_a$, so these are exactly its equal-value classes. In particular, right multiplication by $(1,1)$ pairs $(1,0)$ with $(2,1)$.

This convention uses left cosets: the right coset $H_1(1,0)$ is $\{(1,0),(0,1)\}$, whose two $F$-values are $1$ and $3$; it is not the hidden left coset $C_1$.
